purpose: Add eight source-exact Horatius Bonar excerpts for discipleship, devotion, and sermon application.

defaults.author: Horatius Bonar
defaults.sourceTitle: Follow the Lamb; or, Counsels to Converts
defaults.rightsBasis: This 1875 edition is public domain; each excerpt is verified against the stored OCR and should be checked against the scan before publication.

entries.title: A great thing to be a Christian
entries.text: It is a great thing to be a Christian. The very name is a noble one, beyond all the noble names of earth.
entries.slideText: It is a great thing to be a Christian.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed opening line before explaining the believer's identity and responsibility from Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: Bonar's language is devotional exhortation. Define Christian identity from the cited KJV passages rather than from social status or human merit.

entries.title: Be His living epistles
entries.text: Let men know what a Lord and Master you serve. Be His witnesses; be His mirrors; be His living epistles.
entries.slideText: Be His witnesses; be His mirrors; be His living epistles.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed application after teaching that a believer's conduct should commend Christ to others.
entries.reviewNote: The mirror metaphor is Bonar's illustration. Let the cited KJV texts govern the doctrine of witness and living epistles.

entries.title: Let your life tell
entries.text: Let your life tell your fellow-men what He is, and what He is to you.
entries.slideText: Let your life tell your fellow-men what He is, and what He is to you.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed application for a message about visible faith and a consistent Christian testimony.
entries.reviewNote: A godly life accompanies but does not replace verbal Gospel witness. Explain both from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Continuous following
entries.text: Your whole life is to be one continuous following of the Lord.
entries.slideText: Your whole life is to be one continuous following of the Lord.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed summary line in discipleship preaching about daily, lifelong following of Christ.
entries.reviewNote: This is pastoral application, not a definition of justification. Keep salvation by grace distinct from the believer's obedient walk.

entries.title: Act out your professions
entries.text: Remember what you are, and what God expects at your hand. Act out your own professions, your own faith, your own prayers.
entries.slideText: Act out your own professions, your own faith, your own prayers.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed challenge to move from profession and prayer into obedient action.
entries.reviewNote: Avoid turning the exhortation into works-righteousness. Present obedience as the fruit of faith under the cited KJV texts.

entries.title: Your life is a book
entries.text: Your life is a book; it may be a volume of larger or smaller size; and conversion is but the title-page or the preface.
entries.slideText: Your life is a book; it may be a volume of larger or smaller size
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed illustration of conversion beginning a life of growth and service.
entries.reviewNote: This is an analogy, not a claim that a believer authors salvation. Emphasize God's workmanship and the Spirit's work from Scripture.

entries.title: Written for eternity
entries.text: It is a book written for eternity ; see that it be written well.
entries.slideText: It is a book written for eternity ; see that it be written well.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed companion to Bonar's life-as-a-book illustration when preaching eternal accountability.
entries.reviewNote: The unusual space before the semicolon follows the stored OCR. Check the page scan before public quotation and distinguish reward from salvation.

entries.title: Grace is your strength
entries.text: This grace of God is your strength, as it is your joy; and it is only by abiding in it that you can really live the life of the redeemed.
entries.slideText: This grace of God is your strength, as it is your joy
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed application in preaching about grace as the believer's strength for godly living.
entries.reviewNote: Explain grace from the cited KJV passages. Do not use the quotation to blur justification, sanctification, or the need for obedience.
